headline: A series of Pacific storms brings wet, windy weather and coastal flooding through Wednesday.
summary: A slow-moving storm sitting offshore is steering a series of Pacific storms toward western Washington through much of the week. Winds blow from the southeast ahead of each one. Each storm brings more rain to the lowlands and snow to the mountains. Expect wet, breezy weather through Thursday, with the heaviest rain and flood risk on the Olympic Peninsula and Grays Harbor coast. Coastal flooding and high surf are the biggest worry around Wednesday's high tides, and mountain passes, especially in the North Cascades, will see the most snow. Friday brings a break before winds return next weekend. Forecasters are fairly confident about Wednesday's coastal flooding but less sure of the Wednesday-into-Thursday system and tide timing on the Strait and Sound.
